skill_tree.title: Skill Tree 🧠
skill_tree.earn_more_msg: Answer more scenarios to earn Literacy Points!

mc_1.prompt: Heavy rains are expected in 3 days. Your rice crop is at 90% risk of total loss. Insurance deadline is TODAY.
mc_1.voicePrompt: Heavy rains in 3 days. 90 percent risk of crop loss. Insurance deadline is today. What will you do?

options.A: Buy crop insurance (₹6,000 premium — painful but safe)
options.B: Take instant cash from moneylender (₹10,000, no questions asked)
options.C: Skip insurance, hope the rains are light (30% chance)

mc_2a.prompt: The rains came but your insurance covered 80% of the damage. You spent ₹6,000 but saved ₹48,000. Great decision!
mc_2a.voicePrompt: Insurance covered 80% of the damage. You spent 6,000 but saved 48,000!
mc_2a.lesson: [Skill Tested: Insurance Literacy] Crop insurance costs a painful premium upfront but protects you from catastrophic losses 10x larger.

mc_2b.prompt: The moneylender gave you ₹10,000 fast — but now you owe ₹15,000 at 40% interest. The debt trap begins.
mc_2b.voicePrompt: The moneylender gave 10,000 but now you owe 15,000 at 40% interest. Debt trap!
mc_2b.lesson: Moneylenders charge 30-40% interest. That ₹10,000 becomes ₹15,000 in months. Formal bank loans are only 7%. NEVER borrow from informal lenders.

mc_2c.prompt: The rains were brutal. 70% of your crop destroyed. No insurance, no savings, no backup. You're starting from zero.
mc_2c.voicePrompt: 70% of your crop is destroyed. No insurance. You are starting from zero.
mc_2c.lesson: Gambling on the weather is the #1 reason farmers fall into poverty. ₹6,000 insurance could have saved ₹50,000.

mp_1.prompt: Your wheat harvest is ready. A middleman offers ₹1,100/quintal cash at your door. Mandi price is ₹2,000/q but transport costs ₹4,500 upfront and takes 2 days. Rat risk if you store.
mp_1.voicePrompt: Wheat ready. Middleman offers 1,100 at your door. Mandi is 2,000 but transport costs 4,500. What will you do?

options.B: Pay ₹4,500 upfront to transport to mandi (₹2,000/q)
options.C: Store in barn and wait for higher prices

mp_2a.prompt: You sold at ₹1,100/q and got ₹22,000. Safe, but the middleman exploited you. You lost ₹12,000 potential profit.
mp_2a.voicePrompt: You got 22,000. Safe but the middleman took advantage. You lost 12,000 in potential profit.
mp_2a.lesson: [Skill Tested: Negotiation] Middlemen profit by buying low from desperate farmers. Always check mandi prices on the e-NAM app before accepting any offer.

mp_2b.prompt: The mandi paid ₹2,000/q! After ₹4,500 transport you earned ₹34,000 — ₹12,000 more than the middleman!
mp_2b.voicePrompt: Mandi paid 2,000 per quintal! After transport you earned 34,000. Great decision!
mp_2b.lesson: Transport to the mandi is scary upfront, but yielded 55% more income. Collective transport with other farmers cuts costs further.

mp_2c.prompt: Rats ate 20% of stored grain. Storage fees cost ₹3,500. Prices dropped and you sold for less than the middleman offered.
mp_2c.voicePrompt: Rats ate your grain, storage cost 3,500, and prices dropped. Total disaster.
mp_2c.lesson: Without proper storage (cold storage or government warehouses), waiting is a gamble. Rats and moisture destroy 10-15% of stored grain in India.

sc_1.prompt: Season profit: ₹15,000. Your brother demands ₹10,000 for his wedding — guilt-tripping you hard. Your emergency fund is ₹0. What do you do?
sc_1.voicePrompt: You made 15,000 profit. Brother wants 10,000 for wedding. Emergency fund is zero. What do you do?

options.A: Give ₹10,000 to your brother (keep family happy)
options.B: Refuse and save the full ₹15,000 as emergency fund

sc_2a.prompt: Next season, your child fell sick. Medicine costs ₹8,000. You have only ₹5,000. You must borrow from a moneylender at 30% interest.
sc_2a.voicePrompt: Your child is sick. Medicine costs 8,000. You only have 5,000. You must borrow at 30 percent interest.
sc_2a.lesson: Social pressure to spend is the #1 enemy of savings. An emergency fund of 3-6 months prevents you from falling into a debt trap when life hits hard.

sc_2b.prompt: Next season your child needed medicine. Your emergency fund covered it. No debt needed!
sc_2b.voicePrompt: Excellent! Your emergency fund saved you from a debt trap.
sc_2b.lesson: [Skill Tested: Budget Planning] A healthy emergency fund (₹10,000-₹50,000) is the primary protection for farming families.

sc_2c.prompt: Good balance! Your savings covered 80% of the emergency. Only a small loan was needed.
sc_2c.voicePrompt: A good balance. Your savings covered most of the emergency cost.
sc_2c.lesson: Balancing savings and family needs is wise. Even partial savings significantly reduce crisis impact.

lt_1.prompt: You need ₹30,000 to buy seeds and fertilizer for the season. Where do you borrow?
lt_1.voicePrompt: You need 30,000 to buy seeds and fertilizer. Where do you borrow?

lt_2a.prompt: You repaid ₹32,100 (7% interest after 1 year). Formal credit costs least!
lt_2a.voicePrompt: Great choice! The bank loan was the cheapest and safest option.
lt_2a.lesson: Kisan Credit Card offers loans at 7% p.a. (4% with subsidy). It is the cheapest and most farmer-friendly credit option in India.

lt_2b.prompt: After a bad harvest, you can't repay ₹55,000. Interest compounds at 40%. Two seasons later you owe ₹90,000. The moneylender threatens to seize your land.
lt_2b.voicePrompt: You can't repay 55,000. Interest compounds. You now owe 90,000. The moneylender threatens your land.
lt_2b.lesson: Informal moneylender debt traps families for GENERATIONS. ₹30,000 became ₹90,000 in 2 seasons. KCC bank loan for the same amount costs only ₹32,100.

lt_2c.prompt: SHG loan at 12% was manageable. You repaid ₹33,600. Better than a moneylender!
lt_2c.voicePrompt: The self help group loan was a good middle ground and you repaid it.
lt_2c.lesson: Self-Help Groups are a great community-based alternative to moneylenders. Join or form a local SHG to access collective credit.

ds_1.prompt: The PM-Kisan subsidy of ₹2,000 has been announced. How will you receive it?
ds_1.voicePrompt: The PM-Kisan subsidy of 2,000 has been announced. How will you receive it?

options.A: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to your bank account — free
options.B: Ask a local agent to collect it (₹500 fee, 'for processing')

ds_2a.prompt: The money arrived instantly in your account!
ds_2a.voicePrompt: The money arrived instantly in your account via direct transfer!
ds_2a.lesson: [Skill Tested: Digital Payments] Linking your mobile and Aadhaar to your bank ensures instant, zero-fee direct government transfers.

ds_2b.prompt: The agent took a ₹500 cut. You only received ₹1,500 — and he might have stolen your Aadhaar details too.
ds_2b.voicePrompt: The agent took 500 of your money and may have stolen your identity details.
ds_2b.lesson: [Skill Tested: Digital Payments] Agents steal 25-50% of subsidies. They also harvest Aadhaar data for future scams. Always use DBT directly.

hb_1.prompt: Your cotton harvest is ready. A trader offers ₹5,500/quintal. A cooperative promises ₹6,200 but payment comes in 30 days. What do you do?
hb_1.voicePrompt: Cotton harvest is ready. Trader offers 5,500 now. Cooperative offers 6,200 in 30 days. What will you do?

options.A: Sell to trader now (₹5,500/q, instant payment)
options.C: Negotiate with trader for a higher price

hb_2a.prompt: You got ₹24,000 quickly but the cooperative paid others ₹31,000. You lost ₹7,000 to impatience.
hb_2a.voicePrompt: You got 24,000 but the cooperative paid others 31,000. You lost 7,000.
hb_2a.lesson: [Skill Tested: Negotiation] Private traders exploit urgency. Cooperatives give 10-30% more. Plan your finances so you can wait 30 days.

hb_2b.prompt: Great patience! The cooperative paid ₹31,000 — ₹3,500 more than the trader offered.
hb_2b.voicePrompt: Great patience! The cooperative paid 31,000, which is 3,500 more than the trader offered.
hb_2b.lesson: [Skill Tested: Negotiation] Farmer cooperatives cut out middlemen and share profits with members. Joining one is one of the best financial decisions a farmer can make.

hb_2c.prompt: The trader agreed to ₹5,800/q. A small win! You earned ₹29,000.
hb_2c.voicePrompt: The trader agreed to 5,800. A small win! You earned 29,000.
hb_2c.lesson: [Skill Tested: Negotiation] Always negotiate! Even a small increase per quintal adds up significantly over a full harvest. Research the MSP (Minimum Support Price) before any sale.

eq_1.prompt: A salesman offers a new tractor on EMI: ₹8,000/month for 5 years. Your current monthly income is ₹12,000. Should you buy it?
eq_1.voicePrompt: A salesman offers a tractor on EMI: 8,000 a month. Your income is 12,000. Should you buy it?

options.B: Rent a tractor this season (₹3,000 one-time)
options.C: Form a group with 3 neighbours and buy jointly

eq_2a.prompt: The EMI eats 67% of your income. One bad season and you default on the loan.
eq_2a.voicePrompt: The EMI is 67 percent of your income. You might default on the loan.
eq_2a.lesson: [Skill Tested: Budget Planning] EMI should never exceed 30-40% of your monthly income. A ₹8,000 EMI on a ₹12,000 income leaves no room for food, school fees, or emergencies.

eq_2b.prompt: Smart! Renting saved you from a debt trap. You paid just ₹3,000 and kept ₹9,000 free for other expenses.
eq_2b.voicePrompt: Smart! Renting saved you from a debt trap and kept your cash free.
eq_2b.lesson: [Skill Tested: Budget Planning] Renting equipment makes sense when you don't need it year-round. Custom Hiring Centres (CHC) offer government-subsidised machinery rentals.

eq_2c.prompt: Joint ownership works! Each farmer paid ₹40,000 and sharing the maintenance cost keeps everyone happy.
eq_2c.voicePrompt: Joint ownership works! Sharing the cost keeps everyone happy.
eq_2c.lesson: [Skill Tested: Budget Planning] Collective asset ownership is a cornerstone of rural financial resilience. Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) often provide equipment pools.

fi_1.prompt: The weather forecast shows 90% chance of flash floods next week. Your sugarcane crop worth ₹60,000 is standing in the field. The insurance deadline is TODAY.
fi_1.voicePrompt: Weather forecast shows 90 percent chance of floods. Your 60,000 crop is at risk. Insurance deadline is today.

options.A: Buy insurance NOW (₹4,500 premium — it hurts, but 90% flood risk)
options.B: Skip insurance, harvest early to salvage what you can
options.C: Do nothing — forecasts are wrong all the time, right?

fi_2a.prompt: The floods came. Insurance paid ₹48,000 (80% of crop value). You paid ₹4,500 and saved ₹43,500. Smart move!
fi_2a.voicePrompt: Floods came. Insurance paid 48,000. You paid 4,500. Saved 43,500!
fi_2a.lesson: [Skill Tested: Insurance Literacy] Under PMFBY, ₹4,500 protected a ₹60,000 crop — a 10x return on protection! Always insure before the deadline.

fi_2b.prompt: You harvested early and got ₹25,000 — only 42% of the potential value due to immature crop.
fi_2b.voicePrompt: You harvested early and got 25,000, which is only 42 percent of the value.
fi_2b.lesson: [Skill Tested: Insurance Literacy] Early harvesting due to panic often results in lower quality and price. Insurance allows you to wait for optimal harvest timing without fear.

fi_2c.prompt: The floods destroyed 95% of your crop. No insurance. You lost everything — ₹60,000 crop gone and now ₹30,000 in debt from harvest loans.
fi_2c.voicePrompt: Total loss. 95 percent crop destroyed. 60,000 gone. 30,000 debt. You gambled and lost.
fi_2c.lesson: [Skill Tested: Insurance Literacy] Hoping for the best is NOT a financial strategy. ₹4,500 insurance could have saved you from ₹90,000 in total losses.

up_1.prompt: You sold wheat for ₹45,000 at the mandi. The buyer says: 'I'll pay you ₹44,000 in cash now, or ₹45,000 via UPI in 2 days.' What do you choose?
up_1.voicePrompt: You sold wheat for 45,000. Buyer offers 44,000 cash now, or 45,000 via UPI in 2 days. What will you do?

options.C: Demand cash but ask for full ₹45,000

up_2a.prompt: You got ₹44,000 in cash. But carrying ₹44,000 in cash home is risky — and you lost ₹1,000 for no reason.
up_2a.voicePrompt: You got 44,000 cash, but it's risky to carry and you lost 1,000.
up_2a.lesson: [Skill Tested: Digital Payments] Digital payments are safer than carrying large amounts of cash, fully traceable, and reduce the risk of theft and disputes.

up_2b.prompt: The UPI transfer arrived exactly 2 days later. Full ₹45,000, with a digital receipt for your records!
up_2b.voicePrompt: The UPI transfer arrived! You got the full 45,000 and a digital receipt.
up_2b.lesson: [Skill Tested: Digital Payments] UPI transfers are instant and free. Always get a transaction ID as your receipt. You can also use UPI to pay for seeds and fertilizers directly from dealers.

up_2c.prompt: The buyer walked away. You found another buyer but had to transport again, costing ₹2,000.
up_2c.voicePrompt: The buyer walked away. Finding another buyer cost you 2,000 in transport.
up_2c.lesson: [Skill Tested: Digital Payments] When negotiating, consider the cost of alternatives. Sometimes accepting digital payment and waiting 2 days is smarter than losing the sale.

fs_1.prompt: A man visits your village: 'Pay ₹5,000 registration fee and get ₹1,00,000 subsidy in 1 week!' He has a fake certificate and uniform. He says 'Hurry, only 5 slots left!' What do you do?
fs_1.voicePrompt: A man says pay 5,000 now, get 1 lakh in a week. He seems official. Only 5 slots left. What do you do?

options.A: Pay ₹5,000 quickly before slots fill up
options.B: Ask him to show official .gov.in website proof
options.C: Call local bank or gram panchayat to verify first

fs_2a.prompt: He vanished with your ₹5,000. The 'scheme' was a scam run across 10 villages. You lost your seed money for next season.
fs_2a.voicePrompt: He vanished with 5,000. It was a scam. You lost your seed money for next season.
fs_2a.lesson: [Skill Tested: Fraud Detection] 'Hurry, limited slots' is a classic pressure tactic. NO government scheme asks for advance cash. Report to cybercrime helpline: 1930.

fs_2b.prompt: He couldn't provide a valid .gov.in URL and left quickly! You saved ₹2,000 from a classic scam.
fs_2b.voicePrompt: He couldn't provide a proper website and left. You saved your money!
fs_2b.lesson: [Skill Tested: Fraud Detection] Always verify schemes at pmkisan.gov.in, agricoop.nic.in, or your local Krishi Vigyan Kendra. If there's no official website, it's a fraud.

fs_2c.prompt: The panchayat confirmed it was a scam operating in 3 nearby villages. You alerted your community!
fs_2c.voicePrompt: The panchayat confirmed it was a scam. You protected your community!
fs_2c.lesson: [Skill Tested: Fraud Detection] Community verification is the strongest shield against fraud. Report suspicious persons to the National Cyber Crime Helpline: 1930.

dp_1.prompt: You receive an SMS: 'Your Kisan Credit card is blocked. Share your OTP to reactivate.' What do you do?
dp_1.voicePrompt: You received an SMS. Your card is blocked. Share your OTP to reactivate. What do you do?

options.B: Ignore the SMS — call your bank directly
options.C: Ask a family member for advice first

dp_2a.prompt: ₹35,000 was instantly withdrawn. Your entire season's savings — GONE. Banks NEVER ask for OTPs via phone or SMS.
dp_2a.voicePrompt: 35,000 instantly stolen from your account. Your entire savings gone. Banks never ask for O T P.
dp_2a.lesson: NEVER share your OTP, PIN, or password with ANYONE. Banks will NEVER call asking for OTP. Report fraud immediately to 1930 (National Cybercrime Helpline).

dp_2b.prompt: Smart! The bank confirmed it was a fraud attempt. Your account is safe.
dp_2b.voicePrompt: Smart move! You protected your account from a scammer.
dp_2b.lesson: [Skill Tested: Fraud Detection] Always verify by calling your bank's official number (back of debit card). Real banks NEVER ask for OTP via SMS or calls.

dp_2c.prompt: Your family member recognized it as a scam. Good thinking to ask!
dp_2c.voicePrompt: Good thinking! Your family helped you avoid a scam.
dp_2c.lesson: When in doubt, consult trusted people before acting. Community knowledge is a powerful shield against fraud.

glossary.insurance: Protection against financial loss from crop failure.
glossary.loan: Money borrowed that must be paid back with interest.
glossary.savings: Money set aside for future emergencies.
glossary.interest: The cost of borrowing money or the reward for saving it.
glossary.kharif: Autumn harvest season, dependent on monsoon rains.
glossary.rabi: Spring harvest season, relies on irrigation.
